qns_content.text: The mean free path of a gas molecule is \(8 \times 10^{-7} \, \text{m}\) at 1 atm. What will it be at 0.25 atm if temperature remains constant?

text_solutions:
\(l \propto \frac{1}{n}\), \(n \propto P\). If \(P\) reduces to \(\frac{1}{4}\), \(n\) reduces to \(\frac{1}{4}\), \(l\) increases 4 times.

New \(l = 8 \times 10^{-7} \times 4 = 3.2 \times 10^{-6} \, \text{m}\).

questions.topic: Behaviour of Perfect Gas and Kinetic Theory

qns_content.text: At STP, 22.4 litres of oxygen gas (\(O_2\)) is present. What is the mass of this gas? (Molecular mass of \(O_2 = 32 \, \text{u}\), \(1 \, \text{u} = 1 \, \text{g/mol}\))

text_solutions:
At STP (273 K, 1 atm), 1 mole of any ideal gas occupies 22.4 litres (molar volume).

Given volume = 22.4 litres, so number of moles (\(\mu\)) = \( \frac{22.4}{22.4} = 1 \, \text{mol} \).

Mass = \(\mu \times \text{molecular mass} = 1 \times 32 = 32 \, \text{g} \).

qns_content.text: A gas occupies 67.2 litres at STP. How many molecules are present? (\(N_A = 6.02 \times 10^{23} \, \text{mol}^{-1}\), molar volume at STP = 22.4 litres)

text_solutions:
Number of moles (\(\mu\)) = \(\frac{\text{Volume}}{\text{Molar volume}} = \frac{67.2}{22.4} = 3.0 \, \text{mol}\).

Number of molecules = \(\mu \times N_A = 3.0 \times 6.02 \times 10^{23} = 1.806 \times 10^{24}\).

text_solutions:
Triatomic gas: 6 degrees of freedom, \(C_v = 3 R\).

\(Q = \mu C_v \Delta T = 0.4 \times 3 \times 8.31 \times 15 = 149.58 \, \text{J} \approx 149.6 \, \text{J}\).

questions.topic: Behaviour of Perfect Gas and Kinetic Theory

qns_content.text: A gas occupies a volume of 11.2 litres at STP. How many molecules are present in this gas? (\(N_A = 6.02 \times 10^{23} \, \text{mol}^{-1}\))

text_solutions:
Molar volume at STP = 22.4 litres/mol.

Number of moles (\(\mu\)) = \( \frac{11.2}{22.4} = 0.5 \, \text{mol} \).

Number of molecules = \(\mu \times N_A = 0.5 \times 6.02 \times 10^{23} = 3.01 \times 10^{23} \).

qns_content.text: A gas has a volume of 22.4 litres at STP. How many moles are present if the temperature is raised to 546 K at constant pressure?

text_solutions:
At STP, 22.4 litres = 1 mole.

Charles’ law: \(\frac{V_1}{T_1} = \frac{V_2}{T_2}\), but moles remain constant at constant \(P\).

Initial \(\mu = 1 \, \text{mol}\), remains 1 mole as \(V\) adjusts with \(T\).

qns_content.text: A solid has a molar specific heat capacity of \(24.9 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\). What is the energy per degree of freedom per atom? (\(R = 8.31 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1}\))

text_solutions:
\(C = f \times \frac{R}{2}\), \(24.9 = f \times \frac{8.31}{2}\), \(f = \frac{24.9 \times 2}{8.31} \approx 6\).

Energy per degree of freedom = \(\frac{1}{2} k_B T\), per mole = \(\frac{1}{2} R T\).

For 1 degree of freedom, energy per mole = \(\frac{8.31}{2} = 4.155 \, \text{J mol}^{-1} \text{K}^{-1} \).

qns_content.text: The mean free path of air molecules at STP is \(2.9 \times 10^{-7} \, \text{m}\). If temperature doubles at constant pressure, what is the new mean free path?

text_solutions:
\(l = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2} n \pi d^2}\), \(n = \frac{N}{V}\), and \(PV = Nk_B T\).

At constant \(P\), \(V \propto T\), so \(n \propto \frac{1}{T}\). If \(T\) doubles, \(n\) halves, \(l\) doubles.

New \(l = 2 \times 2.9 \times 10^{-7} = 5.8 \times 10^{-7} \, \text{m} \).

qns_content.text: The mean free path of a gas molecule is \(2 \times 10^{-7} \, \text{m}\) at a certain pressure. If the pressure is doubled, what is the new mean free path? (Assume constant temperature)

text_solutions:
Mean free path \(l = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2} n \pi d^2}\), where \(n \propto P\) at constant \(T\).

If \(P\) doubles, \(n\) doubles, so \(l\) halves.

New \(l = \frac{2 \times 10^{-7}}{2} = 1 \times 10^{-7} \, \text{m} \).
